title: IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL
variant_label: IB Math AA HL Real-Spec Practice
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public IB Math AA HL subject guide. Not a capture of past exam questions.
source_label: IB Math AA HL practice bank

items.stem: Solve the equation log base 2 of x plus log base 2 of (x minus 2) equals 3 for the real value of x.
items.explanation: Combining the logs gives log base 2 of x(x minus 2) equals 3, so x squared minus 2x equals 8 and x equals 4. The root x equals negative 2 is rejected because the log of a negative number is undefined.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: An arithmetic sequence has first term 5 and common difference 3. Work out the value of the tenth term.
items.explanation: The nth term is u_n equals 5 plus (n minus 1) times 3, so u_10 equals 5 plus 9 times 3 equals 32; the other options skip or add one term too many.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: For the quadratic function f of x equals 2x squared minus 8x plus 5, state the x-coordinate of the vertex.
items.explanation: The vertex x-coordinate is minus b divided by 2a, which is 8 divided by 4 equals 2; the other values come from sign errors or from using the constant term.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: An arithmetic series has first term 3 and common difference 4. Find the sum of the first 20 terms.
items.explanation: S_20 equals 20/2 times (2 times 3 plus 19 times 4) equals 10 times 82 equals 820; the others follow from using 20 or 19 terms incorrectly.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: In the expansion of (1 plus 2x) raised to the power 5, find the coefficient of x cubed.
items.explanation: The general term is C(5,r)(2x)^r, so for x cubed r equals 3 and the coefficient is C(5,3) times 2 cubed equals 10 times 8 equals 80; the other values forget the power of 2 or use the wrong binomial coefficient.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: Solve 2 raised to the power (x plus 1) equals 8 raised to the power (x minus 1).
items.explanation: Writing 8 as 2 cubed gives x plus 1 equals 3x minus 3, so 4 equals 2x and x equals 2; the other options come from equating exponents incorrectly.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: An infinite geometric series has first term 8 and common ratio one half. Find its sum.
items.explanation: The sum is a divided by (1 minus r) equals 8 divided by one half equals 16; the others treat the series as finite or use the wrong ratio.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: The polynomial f of x equals x cubed minus 3x squared plus 4x minus 2. Find the remainder when f of x is divided by (x minus 1).
items.explanation: By the remainder theorem the remainder is f(1) equals 1 minus 3 plus 4 minus 2 equals 0, so (x minus 1) is a factor; the other values are partial evaluations.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: The graph of y equals g of x satisfies g of x equals f of (x minus 3) plus 2. Describe the transformation from f to g.
options: Translation 3 units right and 2 units up
Translation 3 units left and 2 units up
Translation 3 units right and 2 units down
items.explanation: Replacing x by x minus 3 shifts the graph 3 units right and adding 2 shifts it 2 units up; the other options reverse a sign or describe the wrong transformation.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: For the rational function y equals (2x plus 1) divided by (x minus 3), state the equation of the horizontal asymptote.
items.explanation: As x tends to infinity the function approaches the ratio of leading coefficients 2/1 equals 2, so y equals 2; the value 3 gives the vertical asymptote, not the horizontal one.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: Find the product (3 plus 2i)(1 minus 4i), giving your answer in the form a plus bi.
items.explanation: Expanding gives 3 minus 12i plus 2i minus 8i squared equals 3 minus 10i plus 8 equals 11 minus 10i; the others mishandle the i squared term or the imaginary coefficients.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations x plus y equals 7 and 2x minus y equals 2.
items.explanation: Adding the equations gives 3x equals 9 so x equals 3 and y equals 4; the other pairs do not satisfy both equations at once.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: The function f is given by f of x equals 3x minus 2. Find its inverse function.
items.explanation: Swapping x and y and rearranging gives y equals (x plus 2) divided by 3; the other options make a sign error or give the reciprocal rather than the inverse.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: State the largest domain of the real function f of x equals the square root of (2x minus 6).
options: x is greater than or equal to 2
x is greater than or equal to 3
x is less than or equal to 3
x is greater than or equal to 6
items.explanation: The radicand must be non-negative, so 2x minus 6 is at least 0 and x is at least 3; the other inequalities come from mis-solving the linear inequality.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: Find the sum of the geometric series 3 plus 6 plus 12 plus ... up to and including the tenth term.
items.explanation: With a equals 3, r equals 2 and n equals 10, S_10 equals 3(2 to the 10 minus 1) equals 3069; the other values use 9 or 10 terms incorrectly.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Algebra and Functions

items.stem: Given f of x equals x cubed minus 6x squared plus 5, find the value of the derivative f prime at x equals 2.
items.explanation: f prime equals 3x squared minus 12x, so f prime at 2 is 12 minus 24 equals negative 12; the others come from using f(2) instead of f prime(2).
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Differentiate the function y equals sine of 3x with respect to x.
items.explanation: The chain rule gives the derivative as 3 cosine of 3x; the others omit the inner derivative, change the sign, or keep the wrong trigonometric function.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Find the indefinite integral of 6x squared with respect to x.
items.explanation: Integrating gives 6 times x cubed over 3, which is 2x cubed plus C; the others fail to divide by the new exponent.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 2 of 3x squared with respect to x.
items.explanation: The antiderivative is x cubed, so the integral is 2 cubed minus 0 cubed equals 8; the others come from evaluating the integrand rather than the antiderivative.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Differentiate the function y equals x squared times e to the power x.
options: x squared e to the power x
e to the power x times (x squared minus 2x)
e to the power x times (x squared plus 2x)
items.explanation: The product rule gives e to the power x times (x squared plus 2x); the others drop one product term or use the wrong sign on the 2x term.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Find the gradient of the tangent to the curve y equals x squared at the point where x equals 3.
items.explanation: The derivative 2x evaluated at 3 equals 6, which is the tangent gradient; 9 is the y-coordinate and the others are arithmetic slips.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Evaluate the limit as x tends to 0 of sine of 5x divided by x.
items.explanation: Using the standard limit sine of kx over x tends to k, the value is 5; the others ignore the argument 5x.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Find the second derivative of y equals x raised to the power 4.
items.explanation: The first derivative is 4x cubed and the second is 12x squared; the others stop at the first derivative or miscalculate the coefficient.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to e of 1 divided by x with respect to x.
items.explanation: The antiderivative is the natural logarithm, so the integral is ln(e) minus ln(1) equals 1; the others confuse the value of e with the logarithm.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Differentiate the function y equals (2x plus 1) raised to the power 5.
items.explanation: The chain rule gives 5 times (2x plus 1) to the fourth times 2, which is 10(2x plus 1) to the fourth; the others miss the inner derivative or the reduced power.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: The function f of x equals x cubed minus 3x has a local maximum. Find the x-coordinate of that local maximum.
items.explanation: Setting f prime equals 3x squared minus 3 equal to 0 gives x equals plus or minus 1; testing signs shows the local maximum is at x equals negative 1.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Find the area enclosed between the curve y equals x squared and the x-axis from x equals 0 to x equals 3.
items.explanation: The area is the integral of x squared from 0 to 3, which is 3 cubed over 3 equals 9; the others evaluate the function or cube incorrectly.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Differentiate the function y equals x divided by (x plus 1).
items.explanation: The quotient rule gives ((x plus 1) minus x) divided by (x plus 1) squared equals 1 divided by (x plus 1) squared; the others make numerator or sign errors.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: A particle has displacement s of t equals t cubed minus 6t squared. Find its acceleration at t equals 2.
items.explanation: Velocity is 3t squared minus 12t and acceleration is 6t minus 12, which at t equals 2 is 0; the others use velocity or a miscalculated derivative.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: Find the indefinite integral of cosine of 2x with respect to x.
options: one half sine of 2x plus C
items.explanation: Integrating gives one half sine of 2x plus C because d/dx of that is cosine of 2x; the others forget to divide by the inner coefficient or change the sign.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Calculus

items.stem: The vectors a equals (2, -1) and b equals (3, 4) are given. Find their scalar product.
items.explanation: The scalar product is 2 times 3 plus (negative 1) times 4 equals 6 minus 4 equals 2; the others add or drop components.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: Find the magnitude of the vector (6, 8).
items.explanation: The magnitude is the square root of 36 plus 64 equals the square root of 100 equals 10; 14 adds the components and 48 multiplies them.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: State the exact value of sine of 30 degrees.
items.explanation: Sine of 30 degrees is 1/2, or 0.5; 0.866 is sine of 60 degrees and 0.577 is tangent of 30 degrees.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: In a triangle, side a equals 8 is opposite angle A equals 30 degrees and angle B equals 45 degrees. Use the sine rule to find side b.
items.explanation: The sine rule gives b equals 8 times sine 45 divided by sine 30 equals 8 times 0.7071 divided by 0.5, which is 11.31; the others invert the ratio or use the wrong angle.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: Two sides of 5 and 7 enclose an angle of 60 degrees. Use the cosine rule to find the length of the third side.
items.explanation: The third side squared is 25 plus 49 minus 2 times 5 times 7 times cosine 60 equals 39, so the side is the square root of 39, about 6.24; the others mishandle the cosine term.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: State the exact value of tangent of 45 degrees.
items.explanation: Tangent of 45 degrees is 1 because sine and cosine are equal at that angle; 1.732 is tangent of 60 degrees and 0 is tangent of 0 degrees.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: Solve cosine of x equals 0.5 for x in the interval from 0 to 180 degrees.
items.explanation: The principal solution is x equals 60 degrees; 30 degrees gives a different cosine value and 120 degrees has cosine negative one half.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: Using the Pythagorean identity, state the value of sine squared of 40 degrees plus cosine squared of 40 degrees.
items.explanation: The identity sine squared plus cosine squared of the same angle always equals 1; the other values contradict that identity.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: The line r equals (1, 2) plus t times the direction (3, -1). Find the point on the line when t equals 2.
items.explanation: Substituting t equals 2 gives (1 plus 6, 2 minus 2) equals (7, 0); the others use t equals 1 or ignore the position vector.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: A triangle has two sides of length 6 and 9 enclosing an angle of 30 degrees. Find its area.
items.explanation: The area is one half times 6 times 9 times sine 30 equals 27 times 0.5 equals 13.5; the others omit the factor of one half or the sine term.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: The vectors (2, k) and (3, -6) are perpendicular. Find the value of k.
items.explanation: Perpendicular vectors have zero scalar product, so 6 minus 6k equals 0 and k equals 1; the other values give a non-zero scalar product.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: State the equation of the circle with centre (2, -3) and radius 5.
options: (x plus 2) squared plus (y minus 3) squared equals 25
(x minus 2) squared plus (y plus 3) squared equals 25
(x minus 2) squared plus (y minus 3) squared equals 25
(x plus 2) squared plus (y plus 3) squared equals 5
items.explanation: The standard form subtracts the centre coordinates and squares the radius, giving (x minus 2) squared plus (y plus 3) squared equals 25; the others reverse signs or forget to square the radius.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: Given sine of x equals 0.6 and cosine of x equals 0.8 for an acute angle x, find sine of 2x.
items.explanation: The double-angle identity gives sine 2x equals 2 sine x cosine x equals 2 times 0.6 times 0.8 equals 0.96; the others forget the factor of 2 or subtract the squares.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: A sector has radius 6 and central angle pi/3 radians. Find the arc length.
items.explanation: Arc length is r times the angle, so 6 times pi/3 equals 2pi; the others multiply or divide by the wrong factor.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: For the function y equals 3 sine of 2x, state its period.
items.explanation: The period is 2pi divided by the coefficient 2, which is pi; the other values confuse the period with the amplitude or forget to divide.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: Find the mean of the five values 4, 7, 9, 10 and 15.
items.explanation: The mean is the total 45 divided by 5 equals 9; 7 and 10 are individual data values rather than the mean.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Find the median of the six values 3, 7, 8, 5, 12 and 9.
items.explanation: In order the values are 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, so the median is the average of the third and fourth equals 7.5; the others pick one middle value only.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the two scores is 7.
items.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes and 6 of them sum to 7, giving 6/36 equals 1/6; the others use too few favourable outcomes.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Events A and B are independent with P(A) equals 0.5 and P(B) equals 0.4. Find P(A and B).
items.explanation: For independent events P(A and B) equals 0.5 times 0.4 equals 0.2; 0.9 adds the probabilities, which is only valid for mutually exclusive events.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Given P(A and B) equals 0.12 and P(B) equals 0.4, find the conditional probability P(A given B).
items.explanation: P(A given B) equals 0.12 divided by 0.4 equals 0.3; the others multiply the values or subtract them.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. Find the expected value of the score.
items.explanation: The expected value is the average (1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 5 plus 6) divided by 6 equals 3.5; the others round or misread the average.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: A variable is normally distributed with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Find the z-score of the value 130.
items.explanation: The z-score is (130 minus 100) divided by 15 equals 2; the others divide by the wrong value or use the mean instead of the difference.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: A binomial variable has n equals 10 trials and probability of success p equals 0.5. Find the number of ways of obtaining exactly 3 successes.
items.explanation: The number of ways is C(10,3) equals 120; 720 is 6 factorial and 30 comes from 10 times 3.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: A binomial variable has n equals 20 trials and probability p equals 0.3. Find its mean.
items.explanation: The mean of a binomial variable is np equals 20 times 0.3 equals 6; the other values square or halve the product.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Find the variance of the data set 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
items.explanation: The mean is 6, the squared deviations sum to 40, and dividing by 5 gives a variance of 8; 40 is the total sum of squares before division.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Find the number of ways of choosing 2 items from a set of 5 distinct items, where order does not matter.
items.explanation: The number of combinations is C(5,2) equals 10; 20 counts ordered pairs, which double-counts each selection.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: A disease affects 1 percent of a population. A test has sensitivity 95 percent and a false-positive rate of 10 percent. Find the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease.
items.explanation: By Bayes the probability is (0.01 times 0.95) divided by (0.01 times 0.95 plus 0.99 times 0.1) equals 0.0095 divided by 0.1085, which is about 0.088; 0.95 wrongly takes the sensitivity as the answer.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: A scatter diagram yields a product-moment correlation coefficient r equals 0.95. Interpret this value.
items.explanation: A value of r close to positive 1 indicates a strong positive linear relationship; correlation alone does not establish causation and a negative value would be near minus 1.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: Find the number of distinct ways to arrange 4 different books on a shelf.
items.explanation: The number of arrangements is 4 factorial equals 24; the other values confuse permutations with powers or partial products.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability

items.stem: For a normal distribution, state the approximate probability that a value lies within two standard deviations of the mean.
items.explanation: Approximately 95 percent of a normal distribution lies within two standard deviations of the mean; 0.68 corresponds to one standard deviation and 0.99 to three.
items.reference: IB Math AA HL Subject Guide - Statistics and Probability
